newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, ask $68 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $64, ask $68 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Central and southern Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet, with light packer bids at $64.00 per cwt passed by owners who were pricing cattle at $67.00-$68.00, according to feedlot sources.
Fed cattle prices this week were expected to be $1.00 to $2.00 higher than last week's sales at $65.00, following USDA's bullishly-construed monthly Cattle on Feed Report on Friday, the dealers said.
The report showed a much-smaller-than-expected number of cattle placed on feed during December than expected.
Light support also was expected from the return of extremely cold wind chill readings in Kansas, the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, cattle feeders said.
Wind speeds of 20 to 25 mph were resulting in wind chill readings of minus 20 degrees Fahrenheit, several feedlot operators in Kansas and the Panhandle said.
The strong winds and cold could slow weight gains and stress cattle following last week's warmer weather, they said.
"The cattle were pretty humped up when I rode through the yard this morning," a Kansas source said.
